The core widgets are implemented in Rust and imported from `pyzed`. They are the
building blocks of the [components](/pyzed/components/overview/).
See the [layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/) guide for sizes, padding and colors.

## Widget

### `Widget`

An immutable node of the UI tree, implemented in Rust. Returned by every widget and component function. Wherever a child is expected you can also pass a string or a number (converted to `text`) or `None` (ignored).

Every widget has `widget.on(...)` (see [Events](/pyzed/guides/events/)) and `widget.style(*styles, **props)`, which styles it like CSS: background, borders, radius, shadow, padding, margin, size and the typography of every text inside. `widget.style_props()` returns what was set. See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/).

## Layout

### `column`

```python
column(
    children=None,
    *,
    spacing=0.0,
    padding=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    align=None,
    max_width=None,
    clip=False,
)
```

Stacks its children vertically.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `children` | List of children. Nested lists are flattened and `None` and `False` are ignored, so you can write `cond and widget`. |
| `spacing` | Space between children, in pixels. |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `align` | Alignment of the children on the cross axis: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. |
| `max_width` | Maximum width in pixels. |
| `clip` | Clips content that overflows the bounds. |

```python
pz.column([pz.text("One"), pz.text("Two")], spacing=8, padding=16)
```

### `row`

```python
row(
    children=None,
    *,
    spacing=0.0,
    padding=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    align=None,
    clip=False,
    wrap=False,
    line_spacing=None,
)
```

Lays out its children horizontally.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `children` | List of children. Nested lists are flattened and `None` and `False` are ignored, so you can write `cond and widget`. |
| `spacing` | Space between children, in pixels. |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `align` | Alignment of the children on the cross axis: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. |
| `clip` | Clips content that overflows the bounds. |
| `wrap` | Line wrapping / moves children to a new row when they don't fit. |
| `line_spacing` | Space between rows when `wrap=True`. |

```python
pz.row([ui.label("Name"), pz.hspace(), ui.button("OK", "ok")], align="center")
```

### `container`

```python
container(
    content=None,
    *,
    padding=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    max_width=None,
    max_height=None,
    align_x=None,
    align_y=None,
    center=False,
    bg=None,
    color=None,
    border_color=None,
    border_width=0.0,
    radius=None,
    shadow=None,
    clip=False,
    gradient=None,
)
```

Wraps a child to give it size, alignment, background, border, radius and shadow.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | The child (or `None` for an empty box, handy as a colored rectangle). |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `max_width` | Maximum width in pixels. |
| `max_height` | Maximum height in pixels. |
| `align_x` | Horizontal alignment: `"start"`/`"left"`, `"center"`, `"end"`/`"right"`. |
| `align_y` | Vertical alignment: `"start"`/`"top"`, `"center"`, `"end"`/`"bottom"`. |
| `center` | Centers the content on both axes and fills all the space. |
| `bg` | Background color (`"#rrggbb[aa]"`, `(r, g, b[, a])` or `"transparent"`). |
| `color` | Text or icon color. |
| `border_color` | Border color. |
| `border_width` | Border width in pixels. |
| `radius` | Corner radius: a number or `(top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left)`. |
| `shadow` | Shadow: `(color, (dx, dy), blur)`. |
| `clip` | Clips content that overflows the bounds. |
| `gradient` | Linear background gradient: `(angle, [colors])` or `(angle, [(position, color), ...])`. |

### `center`

```python
center(content, **kwargs)
```

Centers `content` in all the available space. Equivalent to `container(content, center=True)`.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | Content: a `Widget`, a string or a number (converted to text). |
| `kwargs` | Any `container` parameter. |

### `scrollable`

```python
scrollable(
    content,
    *,
    direction='vertical',
    width=None,
    height=None,
    padding=None,
    id=None,
    anchor_bottom=False,
    rail=None,
    scroller=None,
    scroller_hover=None,
    scrollbar_width=8.0,
    scroller_width=None,
    margin=0.0,
    on_scroll=None,
)
```

Makes its content scrollable.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | Content: a `Widget`, a string or a number (converted to text). |
| `direction` | `"vertical"`, `"horizontal"` or `"both"`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `id` | Stable identifier used to focus or scroll it with a `Command`. |
| `anchor_bottom` | Keeps the scroll pinned to the end (logs, terminals, chats). |
| `rail` | Scrollbar rail color. |
| `scroller` | Scroller color. |
| `scroller_hover` | Scroller color on hover. |
| `scrollbar_width` | Scrollbar width. |
| `scroller_width` | Scroller width (defaults to the scrollbar's). |
| `margin` | Margin between the scrollbar and the content. |
| `on_scroll` | Callable that receives a dict with `x`, `y`, `relative_x`, `relative_y`, `width`, `height`, `content_width` and `content_height`. |

### `stack`

```python

```

| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |

### `rule`

```python
rule(*, vertical=False, thickness=1.0, color=None)
```

A horizontal (or vertical) divider line.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `vertical` | Vertical line instead of horizontal. |
| `thickness` | Thickness in pixels. |
| `color` | Text or icon color. |

### `grid`

```python
grid(
    children=None,
    *,
    columns=None,
    rows=None,
    max_width=None,
    spacing=0.0,
    row_spacing=None,
    height=None,
    aspect_ratio=None,
    width=None,
    padding=None,
    align_x=None,
    align_y=None,
)
```

Lays out its children in a grid. With `columns=3` the columns are equal (or `max_width` fits as many as possible). With track lists (`columns=[200, "1fr", "auto"]`, `rows=...`) it works like a CSS grid: numbers are pixels, `"auto"` fits the content and `"<n>fr"` shares the space left. Wrap children in `pz.cell` to place them and make them span; the rest fill the free cells row by row. See [Layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/#grids).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `children` | List of children. Nested lists are flattened and `None` and `False` are ignored, so you can write `cond and widget`. |
| `columns` | Number of equal columns, or tracks: a list (`[200, "1fr", "auto"]`) or a string (`"200 1fr auto"`). |
| `rows` | Row tracks, like `columns`. Rows beyond the list are `"auto"`. |
| `max_width` | Fits as many columns of at most this width as possible (`columns=<int>` only). |
| `spacing` | Space between cells. |
| `row_spacing` | Space between rows, if different. |
| `height` | With `columns=<int>`: height of each row. With tracks: the grid's height. |
| `aspect_ratio` | Keeps cells at this width/height ratio (`columns=<int>` only). |
| `width` | With `columns=<int>`: pixels. With tracks: the grid's width (default `"fill"`). |
| `padding` | Space around the cells. |
| `align_x` | Horizontal alignment of items in their cells: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`. |
| `align_y` | Vertical alignment of items in their cells. |

```python
pz.grid([pz.cell(header, column=0, row=0, column_span=2), sidebar, content],
        columns=[200, "1fr"], rows=[48, "1fr"], spacing=8, height="fill")
```

### `cell`

```python
cell(
    content,
    *,
    column=None,
    row=None,
    column_span=1,
    row_span=1,
    align_x=None,
    align_y=None,
)
```

Places a child in a track grid: its column and row (from 0) and how many it spans. Children without a cell fill the free cells row by row. Outside a grid it is just the child.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | The widget. |
| `column` | Column index (from 0). |
| `row` | Row index (from 0). |
| `column_span` | Columns it covers. |
| `row_span` | Rows it covers. |
| `align_x` | Horizontal alignment in the cell. |
| `align_y` | Vertical alignment in the cell. |

```python
pz.cell(ui.button("Save"), column=2, row=3, align_x="end")
```

### `flex`

```python
flex(
    children=(),
    *,
    direction='row',
    justify='start',
    align='start',
    gap=0,
    wrap=False,
    padding=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
)
```

Lays children out along one axis, like CSS flexbox, with `justify` on the main axis and `align` on the cross axis. Use `pz.flex_item` to make a child grow or give it a fixed size.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `children` | The widgets, or `pz.flex_item(...)` for children with their own sizing. |
| `direction` | `"row"` or `"column"`. |
| `justify` | `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, `"between"`, `"around"` or `"evenly"`. No effect when a child grows. |
| `align` | Cross-axis alignment: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. |
| `gap` | Space between children. |
| `wrap` | Wraps onto new lines (rows with `justify="start"` only). |
| `padding` | Space around the children. |
| `width` | Width. |
| `height` | Height. |

```python
pz.flex([logo, title, pz.flex_item(search, grow=1), avatar], justify="between", align="center", gap=8)
```

### `flex_item`

```python
flex_item(content, *, grow=1, basis=None, align=None)
```

Sizes a child of `pz.flex`.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | The widget. |
| `grow` | Share of the free space on the main axis (`0` keeps its natural size). |
| `basis` | A fixed main size in pixels, instead of growing. |
| `align` | Cross-axis alignment for this child. |

### `resizable`

```python
resizable(
    content,
    *,
    edge='right',
    size=240.0,
    min_size=80.0,
    max_size=None,
    on_resize=None,
    color=None,
    hover_color=None,
    thickness=1.0,
    handle=8.0,
    width=None,
    height=None,
)
```

A panel whose `edge` can be dragged to resize it. It keeps the size the user drags it to; `on_resize(size)` is called when a drag ends so you can save it. Changing `size` later resets it.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | The panel's content. |
| `edge` | The edge with the handle: `"right"` (a left sidebar), `"left"`, `"top"` (a bottom panel) or `"bottom"`. |
| `size` | Starting width (height for top/bottom edges). |
| `min_size` | Smallest size. |
| `max_size` | Largest size. |
| `on_resize` | Called with the new size when a drag ends. |
| `color` | Line color. |
| `hover_color` | Line color while hovered or dragged. |
| `thickness` | Line thickness. |
| `handle` | Width of the area that can be grabbed. |
| `width` | Width for top/bottom edges. |
| `height` | Height for left/right edges. |

```python
pz.row([pz.resizable(sidebar, edge="right", size=240, on_resize=self.save_width), editor])
```

### `split`

```python
split(
    first,
    second,
    *,
    ratio=0.5,
    on_resize=None,
    vertical=False,
    min_size=80.0,
    min_size_second=None,
    color=None,
    hover_color=None,
    thickness=1.0,
    handle=8.0,
    width=None,
    height=None,
)
```

Two panes with a draggable divider. For the theme style use `ui.split`.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `first` | First pane. |
| `second` | Second pane. |
| `ratio` | Proportion of the first pane (0–1). The split keeps the ratio the user drags to until this changes. |
| `on_resize` | Callable that receives the new ratio while dragging. |
| `vertical` | Stacks the panes top/bottom. |
| `min_size` | Minimum size of the first pane. |
| `min_size_second` | Minimum size of the second pane. |
| `color` | Divider color. |
| `hover_color` | Divider color on hover or while dragging. |
| `thickness` | Line thickness. |
| `handle` | Width of the draggable area. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |

### `pin`

```python
pin(content, *, x=0.0, y=0.0, width=None, height=None)
```

Places `content` at `(x, y)` inside a box. Use it in a `stack` to position popovers and context menus.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | Content: a `Widget`, a string or a number (converted to text). |
| `x` | Horizontal position. |
| `y` | Vertical position. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |

### `responsive`

```python
responsive(function)
```

Builds its content with `function(width, height)` using the space actually available, so the layout can adapt (for example, hiding a sidebar when the window is narrow).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `function` | Function that receives `(width, height)` and returns a widget. |

### `FlexItem`

```python
class FlexItem
```

A child of `pz.flex` with its own sizing; made with `pz.flex_item`.

## Text and icons

### `text`

```python
text(
    content,
    *,
    size=None,
    color=None,
    font=None,
    weight=None,
    italic=False,
    line_height=None,
    align_x=None,
    align_y=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    wrap=True,
)
```

A piece of text.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `content` | Content: a `Widget`, a string or a number (converted to text). |
| `size` | Font size. |
| `color` | Text or icon color. |
| `font` | `"sans"` (IBM Plex Sans), `"mono"`, `"icons"`, `"serif"` or the name of a family loaded with `load_font`. |
| `weight` | `"thin"`, `"light"`, `"normal"`, `"medium"`, `"semibold"`, `"bold"`, `"black"` or a number (100–900). |
| `italic` | Italic. |
| `line_height` | Line height relative to the size (1.0, 1.5…). |
| `align_x` | Horizontal alignment: `"start"`/`"left"`, `"center"`, `"end"`/`"right"`. |
| `align_y` | Vertical alignment: `"start"`/`"top"`, `"center"`, `"end"`/`"bottom"`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `wrap` | Line wrapping. With `False` the text doesn't wrap. |

### `icon`

```python
icon(name, *, size=16, color=None)
```

A [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icon. `color` defaults to the surrounding text color.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Icon name (`pyzed icons` lists them). |
| `size` | Size in pixels. |
| `color` | Color. |

```python
pz.icon("folder", size=16, color="#74ade8")
```

### `svg`

```python
svg(
    source,
    *,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    color=None,
    content_fit=None,
    opacity=1.0,
    rotation=0.0,
)
```

An SVG image.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | Path to an `.svg`, the SVG code as a string (starting with `<`) or `bytes`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `color` | If given, tints the whole SVG with that color (useful for monochrome icons). |
| `content_fit` | `"contain"`, `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"none"` or `"scale-down"`. |
| `opacity` | Opacity from 0 to 1. |
| `rotation` | Rotation in degrees. |

## Images and content

### `image`

```python
image(
    source,
    *,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    content_fit=None,
    filter='linear',
    opacity=1.0,
    radius=0.0,
    rotation=0.0,
    scale=1.0,
    size=None,
)
```

A bitmap image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP…) from a path or `bytes`, or raw RGBA pixels.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | File path, `bytes` of the encoded file, or raw RGBA pixels with `size=(width, height)`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `content_fit` | `"contain"`, `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"none"` or `"scale-down"`. |
| `filter` | `"linear"` (smooth) or `"nearest"` (crisp pixels, for pixel art). |
| `opacity` | Opacity from 0 to 1. |
| `radius` | Corner radius. |
| `rotation` | Rotation in degrees. |
| `scale` | Scale. |
| `size` | `(width, height)` when `source` is raw RGBA pixels. |

```python
pz.image("photo.jpg", width=320, content_fit="cover", radius=8)
```

### `image_viewer`

```python
image_viewer(
    source,
    *,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    min_scale=0.25,
    max_scale=10.0,
    scale_step=0.1,
    filter='linear',
    size=None,
)
```

An image you can pan (by dragging) and zoom (mouse wheel), like Iced's viewer.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | File path, `bytes` of the encoded file, or raw RGBA pixels with `size=(width, height)`. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `min_scale` | Minimum zoom. |
| `max_scale` | Maximum zoom. |
| `scale_step` | How much the zoom changes per wheel step. |
| `filter` | `"linear"` (smooth) or `"nearest"` (crisp pixels, for pixel art). |
| `size` | `(width, height)` for raw RGBA pixels. |

### `rich_text`


Text made of spans with different styles. Plain strings are unstyled spans.

| `wrap` | Line wrapping / moves children to a new row when they don't fit. |

```python
pz.rich_text(["Click ", pz.span("here", color="#74ade8", underline=True, link=self.open), " to open."])
```

### `span`

```python
span(
    text,
    *,
    color=None,
    size=None,
    font=None,
    weight=None,
    italic=False,
    bg=None,
    radius=0.0,
    padding=None,
    underline=False,
    strikethrough=False,
    link=None,
)
```

A styled span for `rich_text`. With `link`, clicking it sends (or calls) that value.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | The text. |
| `color` | Text or icon color. |
| `size` | Size. |
| `font` | Font of the span or text (family name, e.g. `"IBM Plex Mono"`). |
| `weight` | Font weight: `"normal"`, `"medium"`, `"semibold"` or `"bold"`. |
| `italic` | If `True`, the span is drawn in italics. |
| `bg` | Background color (`"#rrggbb[aa]"`, `(r, g, b[, a])` or `"transparent"`). |
| `radius` | Background radius. |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `underline` | Underline. |
| `strikethrough` | Strikethrough. |

### `canvas`

```python
canvas(
    shapes=None,
    *,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    id=None,
    on_press=None,
    on_release=None,
    on_right_press=None,
    on_move=None,
    on_scroll=None,
    cursor=None,
)
```

A 2D drawing surface. `shapes` is a list created with [`pyzed.draw`](/pyzed/reference/draw/). Mouse callbacks receive coordinates relative to the canvas. With an `id`, the geometry is cached between frames and only recomputed when the shapes change. See the [drawing with canvas](/pyzed/guides/canvas/) guide.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `shapes` | List of `pyzed.draw` shapes (nested lists are accepted). |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `id` | Enables the geometry cache. |
| `on_press` | Callable that receives `(x, y)` on press. |
| `on_release` | Callable that receives `(x, y)` on release. |
| `on_right_press` | Callable that receives `(x, y)` on right click. |
| `on_move` | Called with `(x, y)` when the mouse moves. |
| `on_scroll` | Callable that receives `(dx, dy)` in lines when the wheel is used. |
| `cursor` | Mouse cursor (`"crosshair"`, `"pointer"`…). |

### `code_editor`

```python
code_editor(
    id,
    text='',
    *,
    language='txt',
    size=14.0,
    line_height=None,
    font=None,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    padding=None,
    syntax=None,
    bg=None,
    color=None,
    selection_color=None,
    placeholder=None,
    placeholder_color=None,
    gutter=True,
    gutter_color=None,
    gutter_active_color=None,
    gutter_width=None,
    markers=None,
    wrap=False,
    on_change=None,
    on_cursor=None,
    active_line=None,
    scrollbar_color=None,

    capture_keys=None,
    on_scroll=None,
    auto_close=False,
    folding=False,
    minimap=None,
    minimap_thumb=None,
    cursor_shape='bar',
    cursor_width=2.0,
    cursor_blink=True,

```

A code editor with syntax highlighting, line numbers and git markers, based on Iced's
`text_editor`. It is **uncontrolled**: `text` is only the initial value for that `id`; the
text, cursor and history live in Rust. Use `Command.set_editor_text` to replace it.
For the Zed style use [`ui.editor`](/pyzed/components/code/).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifies the buffer. Reuse it to keep state across renders. |
| `text` | Initial text. |
| `language` | Language extension or name (`"py"`, `"rs"`, `"json"`…). |
| `size` | Font size. |
| `line_height` | Line height in pixels. |
| `font` | Family (monospace by default). |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `padding` | Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`. |
| `syntax` | Map of TextMate scopes to colors (provided by `Theme.syntax_scopes()`). |
| `bg` | Background color (`"#rrggbb[aa]"`, `(r, g, b[, a])` or `"transparent"`). |
| `color` | Text or icon color. |
| `selection_color` | Selection color. |
| `placeholder` | Hint text shown when empty. |
| `placeholder_color` | Placeholder color. |
| `gutter` | Shows line numbers. |
| `gutter_color` | Line number color. |
| `gutter_active_color` | Color of the cursor line's number. |
| `gutter_width` | Gutter width (automatic by default). |
| `markers` | `{line: color}` for git markers in the gutter (lines from 1). |
| `wrap` | Line wrapping. |
| `on_change` | Callable that receives the full text after each edit. |
| `on_cursor` | Callable that receives `(line, column)`, from 1. |
| `active_line` | Background color of the cursor line. |
| `scrollbar_color` | Scrollbar color. |
| `annotations` | `{line: "text"}` or `{line: ("text", color)}`: virtual text at the end of the line (code lens, diagnostics). |
| `whitespace` | Draws spaces as `·` and tabs as `→` in this color. |
| `tab_size` | Tab inserts spaces up to the next multiple; Enter keeps the indentation; Backspace removes a level. |
| `capture_keys` | Keys the editor leaves to the app's `on_key` (`"up"`, `"enter"`…), e.g. while a completion list is open. |
| `on_scroll` | Called on scroll. |
| `auto_close` | Typing a bracket or quote also inserts its closing pair. |
| `folding` | Fold chevrons in the gutter and Ctrl+Shift+[ / ]. |
| `minimap` | Width of the minimap in pixels (`None`: no minimap). |
| `minimap_thumb` | Color of the minimap's visible-area highlight. |
| `cursor_shape` | `"bar"`, `"block"`, `"underline"` or `"hollow"`. |
| `cursor_width` | Width of the bar cursor. |
| `cursor_blink` | Whether the cursor blinks. |
| `cursor_color` | Cursor color. |
| `on_zoom` | Callable that receives `1`, `-1` or `0` for Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+wheel. |
| `on_action` | Callable that receives the name of each editor action that runs (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`…). |
| `highlights` | Ranges painted behind the text (search results): `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends. |
| `highlight_color` | Color of `highlights`. |
| `match_brackets` | Outlines the bracket that matches the one next to the cursor. |
| `selection_highlight` | Highlights the other occurrences of the selected text. |

## Styles

### `Style`

```python
class Style
```

A reusable set of style properties for `widget.style(...)`, a component's `style=` or `App.style`. Combine styles with `|` (the right one wins). See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `styles` | Styles, dicts or style names to start from. |
| `props` | Properties: `background`, `color`, `font`, `weight`, `italic`, `size`, `line_height`, `border_color`, `border_width`, `border` (`(width, color)`), `radius`, `shadow`, `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `align_x`, `align_y`, `clip`. Colors may be theme tokens. |

```python
card = pz.Style(background="panel", border=(1, "border"), radius=8, padding=12)
pz.column([...]).style(card | pz.Style(shadow=("#0006", (0, 4), 12)))
```

**Methods and properties**

#### `Style.get`

```python
Style.get(key, default=None)
```

Returns a property's value (aliases accepted), or `default` when it is not set.

#### `Style.merge`

```python
Style.merge(*styles, **props)
```

A new style with `styles` and `props` on top of this one.

#### `Style.without`

```python
Style.without(*keys)
```

A new style without these properties.

#### `Style.text`

```python
Style.text()
```

Only the text properties (what a style passes down to the texts inside).

#### `Style.to_dict`

```python
Style.to_dict()
```

JSON-friendly properties (gradients and paints become dicts).

#### `Style.from_dict`

```python
@classmethod
Style.from_dict(data)
```

Builds a style from data made by `to_dict` (aliases accepted).

### `define_style`

```python
define_style(name, *styles, **props)
```

Names a style so widgets can use it by name: `widget.style("card")`. Returns it.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The style's name. |
| `styles` | Styles to merge. |
| `props` | Properties on top. |

### `set_style`

```python
set_style(*styles, **props)
```

Sets the global style for every window, under each window's `style`. Without arguments it clears it.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `styles` | Styles to merge. |
| `props` | Properties on top. |

### `Gradient`

```python
class Gradient
```

A linear gradient for backgrounds. Angles follow CSS: 0 up, 90 right, 180 (the default) down. Up to 8 stops.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `stops` | Colors, spread evenly, or `(offset, color)` pairs with offsets from 0 to 1. |
| `angle` | Direction in degrees. |

```python
pz.container(None, height=80).style(background=pz.Gradient(["#f97316", "#7c3aed"], angle=90))
```

**Methods and properties**

#### `Gradient.to_value`

```python
Gradient.to_value()
```

`(angle, [(offset, "#rrggbbaa"), ...])`, the form widgets take as `gradient=`.

#### `Gradient.to_dict`

```python
Gradient.to_dict()
```

Returns the gradient as JSON-ready data: `{"type": "linear", "angle", "stops"}`.

### `Mask`

```python
class Mask
```

An opacity mask for a `Paint`: how visible the fill is along a direction. On a gradient it follows the gradient's direction.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `stops` | Opacities (0 to 1), spread evenly, or `(offset, opacity)` pairs. |
| `angle` | Direction when the fill is a plain color. |

**Methods and properties**

#### `Mask.at`

```python
Mask.at(offset)
```

Returns the opacity (0 to 1) at `offset` (0 to 1), interpolating between stops.

#### `Mask.to_dict`

```python
Mask.to_dict()
```

Returns the mask as JSON-ready data: `{"angle", "stops"}`.

### `Paint`

```python
class Paint
```

A fill: a color or `Gradient` with an overall opacity and an optional `Mask`. Works anywhere a background does.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `fill` | A color or a `Gradient`. |
| `opacity` | 0 to 1, multiplies the fill's own alpha. |
| `mask` | A `pz.Mask`. |

```python
pz.Paint("#3b82f6", opacity=0.8, mask=pz.Mask([1, 0]))  # fades out downwards
```

**Methods and properties**

#### `Paint.resolve`

```python
Paint.resolve()
```

`(color, gradient)`: what a container draws (one of them is `None`).

#### `Paint.to_dict`

```python
Paint.to_dict()
```

Returns the paint as JSON-ready data: `fill`, `opacity` and `mask` when there is one.

### `global_style`

```python
global_style()
```

The style set with `set_style` (`None` if none).

### `named_styles`

```python
named_styles()
```

The styles defined with `define_style`, by name.

### `apply_global`

```python
apply_global(view, style=None)
```

`view` with a window's global style: text properties fill in what texts leave unset.

### `themed`

```python
themed(theme, style)
```

`theme` with a global style's text color, background, border color, size and radius.

### `to_hex`

```python
to_hex(color)
```

Any color as `"#rrggbb"` or `"#rrggbbaa"` (theme tokens resolved).

### `paint_from_dict`

```python
paint_from_dict(data)
```

Rebuilds a `Gradient` or `Paint` saved with `to_dict()`.
